records.name: Wynnefield Heights Community Association
records.summary: Neighbors in Wynnefield Heights who work together on local issues. They hold community meetings, run youth and environment projects, and talk with public officials on behalf of residents.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly community meeting on Zoom, take part in youth events or neighborhood improvement projects, or become a member.

schedule.text: Community meetings on Zoom each month. The September 2026 meeting was on September 10 from 6:30 to 8 pm.

cost.text: Membership and donations are offered. The membership cost is not stated.

first_step.how: Register for the next community meeting on the group's site, or email the group to ask about membership
first_step.basis: Meetings are public and open to registration on the group's own site, and the group offers membership

records.notes: Formerly the Wynnefield Heights Civic Association, per the homepage. Registration for the September 2026 meeting was closed when checked. The site menu links to a monthly meeting, but no regular day is stated.

records.name: Wynnefield Community Neighborhood Association
records.summary: Wynnefield neighbors who run community events, youth activities and neighborhood preservation work. They also hold public meetings on zoning and development in the area.
records.what_you_do: Come to a bike ride, job fair or other event, join the Neighborhood Preservation Committee, or apply for membership through the group's site.

schedule.text: Virtual community meetings on Zoom, held bi-monthly. Events are posted by date, such as a job fair on September 9, 2026 and a zoning meeting on September 14, 2026.

cost.text: Membership is by application. Event costs are not stated.

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-598-2410, or use the JOIN US option on the group's site to apply for membership
first_step.basis: Events and public meetings are open to neighbors, and the site posts a membership application

records.notes: The site lists a feasibility survey open through September 30, 2026. No email is published. In-person events are held at a commercial event studio on North 54th Street, so no group street address is recorded. A business curfew petition is mentioned with no date.

records.name: West Belmont Civic Association
records.summary: Neighbors in West Belmont who speak up on planning, zoning and development, and who work on block problems such as trash, graffiti and abandoned cars.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly meeting at the church on Ogden Street to raise a problem or hear about local planning, or join the mailing list.

schedule.text: Monthly evening meetings at 6 pm on a Tuesday. The site gives both the first and the fourth Tuesday, so check with the group before you go.

locations.label: Monthly meetings at New Church Down the Way Ministries

cost.text: Cost is not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Come to a monthly meeting at the church on Ogden Street, or sign up on the group's mailing list
first_step.basis: Meetings have a published place, and the site invites residents to bring problems and join the mailing list

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so the status rests on a working site alone. The site gives two different meeting weeks. The street address printed under contact information is not recorded because it may be a private home; the church meeting place is used instead. The email and phone are as the group prints them, and the email is the president's address on the group's own domain.

records.name: Mantua Worldwide Community
records.summary: Neighbors in Mantua who clean up streets, plant gardens and teach young people how things grow. The group also hosts arts and health events.
records.what_you_do: Show up for a neighborhood cleanup or greenup, join the Garden Club (open to youth and adults), or buy a ticket to a garden party.

schedule.text: About four to six cleanups a year, with dates passed to volunteers. The Garden Club's date and time were still to be set on the site.

cost.text: A 2026 garden party ticket was $25 and had to be reserved ahead. Other costs are not stated.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page on the group's site to ask about the next cleanup or the Garden Club start date
first_step.basis: Cleanups are announced by email and word of mouth, and the Garden Club start date is not yet set, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: Newest dated evidence is a February 20, 2026 Spotlight PA profile, which also places the cleanups in Mantua. The group's own site lists a June 2026 item marked TBD and an invitation-only garden party. The site gives only a P.O. box, which is not recorded, and a ticket inquiry address, which is not recorded either.

records.name: Mt. Vernon Manor CDC
records.summary: A community development group for Mantua and East Parkside. It runs a weekly food pantry, helps residents with housing, utilities, taxes and jobs, and builds and rents affordable homes.
records.what_you_do: Sign in for the Wednesday morning food pantry, call the office for help with housing, benefits, tax prep or jobs, or sign up for the newsletter.

schedule.text: Food pantry every Wednesday at 9 am, with sign-in. The office is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 3 pm.

locations.label: Food pantry and services (street address not printed on the site)
Food pantry and services (street address not printed on the site)

cost.text: Costs for the pantry and services are not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Sign in for the Wednesday 9 am food pantry, or call the office Monday to Friday, 9 am to 3 pm, about housing, benefits or jobs
first_step.basis: The site lists a weekly sign-in time, office hours and a phone number, and anyone can subscribe to the newsletter

records.notes: The site names Mantua, Powelton and East Parkside as the areas served. Powelton is not recorded here. The newest dated item is an early 2026 housing item, stored as a bare year. Pantry eligibility rules are not stated on the page.

records.name: SuggaMamas Diabetes Prevention and Management
records.summary: A nonprofit that teaches people about diabetes prevention and self care through a boot camp, pool exercise, cooking and wellness workshops, and men's health forums.
records.what_you_do: Ask about the Boot Camp Experience or a workshop through the Get Involved form or by phone. The site says visits are by appointment.

schedule.text: Programs are offered by appointment. The site lists no current dates.

cost.text: Program cost is not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Use the Get Involved form on the group's site, or call the office to ask about the Boot Camp Experience
first_step.basis: Visits are by appointment and the site lists no open sessions, so the way in is not clear

records.notes: The newest dated item is a September 2022 grant announcement on the site. No 2023 to 2026 dates were found, so the status is dormant. Recorded because the contact details on the site are current. The owner may decide to hold dormant records.

records.name: Centennial Parkside Community Development Corporation
records.summary: A community development group for East Parkside, made up of residents, business owners and development partners, that works to preserve and revitalize the neighborhood.
records.what_you_do: Read the group's information page to learn about its work, then call or email the office to ask how to take part.

schedule.text: No meeting schedule is listed on the site.

first_step.how: Call 267-225-8356 or email info@centennialparkside.org to ask how to get involved
first_step.basis: The site invites neighbors to learn about getting involved but gives no meeting schedule or membership steps

records.notes: The three dated items on the site are from early and September 2023, the latest a job posting for an executive director. No later dates were found, so the status is dormant. The owner may decide to hold dormant records.

records.name: Educated Sistas Association
records.summary: A group that supports women and girls through learning and college events, with quarterly meetings and a way to volunteer or donate.
records.what_you_do: Register for an event, sign up for the monthly email update, or contact the group about volunteering.

schedule.text: Quarterly meetings. The newest dated listing on the site is a January 20, 2024 meeting from 5 to 6:30 pm at 4036 W Girard Ave.

first_step.how: Sign up for the monthly email update or contact the group to ask about the next event
first_step.basis: Event registration and volunteering are listed, but the site shows no current dates, so the way in is not clear

records.notes: The newest dated listing is a January 20, 2024 quarterly meeting at 4036 W Girard Ave, shown as an event location, not a mailing address. The site also still lists 2018 and 2019 college fairs as upcoming, so it is out of date. Neighborhood is not stated, so the record is placed by address only. The owner may decide to hold dormant records.

notes: Budget: all 6 WebSearch calls used (cap reached), and about 47 WebFetch calls of 60. Result: 8 records, well short of the 20 to 40 target. Most in-slice leads with a website either do not resolve, return server errors, or are placeholders, and the search budget went to groups that have no site. Verdicts: 8 publish (4 active, 1 probably_active, 3 dormant). Status counts: active WHCA, WCNA, Mantua Worldwide, MVM CDC; probably_active West Belmont; dormant SuggaMamas, Centennial Parkside CDC, Educated Sistas. Checked but not recorded: Belmont Plateau Trails Alliance (site says coming soon, no dates or join steps); CHARLES Foundation (youth programs, newest dated item June 2022, no address on site); Community Health and Gardens (garden, but no neighborhood, dates or address on site); Good Shepherd Community Church (no programs or dates; copyright only); Christian Resources and Development (site under construction, no address); PZRC (West Philadelphia wide research group, no dates or address); CHANGE counseling and workshops (service provider, no dates, Lancaster Ave address); Terrence L. Gore Art of Healing (no neighborhood, dates or contact); HopePHL (citywide social services, no dated items); Cathedral Park CDC (housing focus, neighborhood and dates not stated); Philadelphia Caribbean Festival (citywide, 2026 festival listed, headquarters not stated); Philadelphia Chaveirim (help line only, no neighborhood); UAC (Urban Affairs Coalition, a nonprofit hub, not the Parkside association); Business Association of West Parkside (business group, out of scope). Friends of Woodside Park uses the Wynnefield Heights site, so it is a duplicate. Out of slice and not checked: Cedar Park Neighbors, Garden Court Community Garden, Cobbs Creek Ambassadors, Friends of Malcolm X Park, Friends of Carroll Park, Overbrook West Neighbors, Overbrook Farms Club, Overbrook Park Townwatch. Data issues for the lead owner: the city and IRS leads list wynnefield.org, belmontalliance.org, phllypumtrack.org and westparkcutural.org, which do not resolve, so those lead websites should be corrected or dropped. Belmont is listed under the West district in data/vocab/neighborhoods.yaml, not West Park; I used the neighborhood belmont as briefed. The Mantua record uses neighborhood mantua from the group's name and a Spotlight PA profile; the group's own site does not name a neighborhood.
